what_happened: Dispatch named three scripts as sharing the invocation-refusal defect; direct empirical reproduction (running each from both the source-store and deployed paths, including a full verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow run diffed byte-for-byte) showed verify-deploy.sh is unaffected -- only check-extension-docs.sh and sync-manifest-scripts.sh actually refuse. This matched task 434's own phase-3-progress.json ground truth exactly, avoiding a wasted fix to verify-deploy.sh in the plan phase.

Research settled the (a)-vs-(b) choice empirically (byte-identical output with the documented override; loud failure even with a wrong root), so planning needed no re-litigation of the dispatch's central question and went straight to mechanism design.

The research report's suggested shape (a new function inside deploy-root-guard.sh, called only by the two in-scope scripts) is not realizable: the guard is a straight-line sourced fragment that exits during the source, so a caller cannot source it to obtain a function without first triggering the refusal. The plan substitutes an opt-in variable gating a new branch inside the guard's existing refusal path, preserving the report's intent (additive, opt-in-only) within that constraint.

First --only run of the 52-suite dependent set for deploy-root-guard.sh showed a transient, non-reproducing failure in test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh (classified NEW); it passed standalone and on a full rerun of the same --only selection, leaving only the pre-existing EXPECTED failure test-guard-git-push.sh. No code change was made in response; treated as pre-existing suite flakiness under concurrent load, not caused by the deploy-root-guard.sh edit.

deploy-headless.sh's inline fast-gate verification (Gate 22, lint-shellcheck.sh) caught 3 real SC2034 ('appears unused') findings introduced by Phase 1/2's cross-file variable handoff: DEPLOY_ROOT_GUARD_SELF_CORRECT set in check-extension-docs.sh and sync-manifest-scripts.sh is only read after being sourced into deploy-root-guard.sh (a different file, invisible to shellcheck's per-file analysis), and REPO_ROOT assigned inside deploy-root-guard.sh's acceptance branch is only consumed by the sourcing caller after the guard returns. Fixed with a one-line inline '# shellcheck disable=SC2034' plus reason at each of the 3 sites, per lint-shellcheck.sh's own stated remedy (never a file- or repo-level disable). Confirmed by re-running the gate before the second deploy-headless.sh attempt: 0 findings.
